lines.say: Does caffeine actually make you stronger?
All day, a chemical called adenosine builds up in your brain and makes you tired.
Caffeine has almost the same shape. It sits in adenosine's spot and blocks it.
So you feel less tired, and hard sets feel easier.
Studies show small boosts in strength, power and endurance.
Doses that work are about three to six milligrams per kilo, about an hour before training.
Start at the low end. Too much brings jitters and a racing heart.
And skip it late in the day, or it can wreck your sleep.
